research_rationale:
EO 8078 (April 4, 1939, Franklin D. Roosevelt) "Amending the Foreign Service Regulations of the United States" is read in full in the held Federal Register text (printed number 8078). Under section 1752 of the Revised Statutes it amends the Tariff of United States Foreign Service Fees in section V-15 of the Foreign Service Regulations: item 8 (a Chinese certificate fee of $10.00), item 9 (a limited entry certificate with no fee) and item 41 (a fee for certifying the correctness of a copy). The order states no term. EO 8396 (April 18, 1940), held Federal Register text, lists EO 8078 among the Executive orders it revokes. That is the first end.

The amendment inserted standing text into a set of regulations or rules; the claim treats that standing amendment as the order's continuing command, ended by the express revocation. The alternative reading, that the amending command was fully performed on signing, is disclosed for the reviewer; it would not change the whole-order end date.","independent_command_check":"No independent command survives. savings.reason: Fees lawfully charged under the amended tariff between April 4, 1939 and April 18, 1940 were charged under valid regulations and are accrued effects. The held EO 8396 text neither mentions section V-15 nor the three fee items and does not say whether the fee text survives in the Foreign Service Regulations after the revocation of the amending order; no held source shows the post-1940 fee text, which is a disclosed gap and not a finding.
